A login with no password, and the same server refusing one

week-14 — the positive and the negative, from the client inside the network
$ az vm run-command invoke -g rg-pgnopass-lab-dev-scus-001 -n vm-app-wk14-dev-scus-001 \
    --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$(cat connect.sh)"

# connect.sh, running on the client. The credential is minted on demand for
# the VM's own identity and never stored anywhere.
export PGPASSWORD=$(curl -sS -H Metadata:true \
  "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01\
&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net&client_id=$CLIENT_ID" \
  | jq -r .access_token)

psql "host=psql-wk14-dev-scus-001.postgres.database.azure.com \
      user=id-app-wk14-dev-scus-001 dbname=orders sslmode=require" \
     -c "select 'connected-as='||current_user"

    connected-as=id-app-wk14-dev-scus-001

# THE CONTROL. Same host, same user, a password instead of a token.
$ PGPASSWORD=not-a-real-password psql "host=... user=id-app-wk14-dev-scus-001 ..."

    psql: error: connection to server at
    "psql-wk14-dev-scus-001.postgres.database.azure.com" (10.60.1.4), port 5432
    failed: FATAL:  The access token has invalid format. Try again after making
    sure that the token is passed exactly as returned by the authentication
    endpoint.

# And as the local administrator a server like this usually has:
$ PGPASSWORD=whatever psql "host=... user=pgadmin ..."

    failed: FATAL:  password authentication failed for user "pgadmin"

# The first refusal is the sharper one: the server does not evaluate the
# string as a password at all, it tries to parse it as a token. The second
# role does not exist, because no administrator_login was ever set.
